minutes.headline: Commission authorized a beaver consultant and a boundary-sign purchase; the Cove Road owner will remove his shed in spring.
minutes.summary: A short Zoom meeting of the Conservation Commission. It heard from the owner at 23 Cove Road, who agreed to take down a shed, and voted on two small purchases. It also reviewed the timber rights fund balance, encroachment letters, and a carpet replacement at Ellis Road.

public_comment.topic: The owner of 23 Cove Road described his plan with the DPW director on drainage and culvert flooding. He said the greenhouse and shed will come down in spring.

budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant offered half price for the Commission, quoted as under a set amount.
The chair reviewed the fund's activity since 2017 and the projected balance after the beaver work and the local grant match.
A little over two thousand dollars remains on two purchase orders, possibly usable for kiosks and bridge repair.
A purchase order to the regional planning commission is likely unnecessary because the town's free GIS hours may be used again, returning the money to the fund.
The harvest is not expected until mid-summer because of ground conditions, so the expected revenue should not be counted on soon.
A purchase of 250 custom markers was proposed and then approved with a spending cap.
Quotes are being gathered. The first includes subfloor repair, and a rough estimate was given for the subfloor fix.

decisions.decision: A new enforcement order will be issued for 23 Cove Road. It will be closed once the shed is down and staff confirm.
123 Farm Hill Road is removed from the encroachment list. 26 Lopez/Mopus Road stays on until it is inspected.
The chair and Anna will contact the new facilities director for help with the Ellis Road carpet work.
A report on the Haws gift fund, like the timber rights fund report, will be prepared with Rebecca Manley.
48 Oak Ridge is scheduled for the March 1st meeting. 454 Pine Grove still needs a full submittal.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted by roll call to authorize hiring a beaver consultant in the spring to look at the road to the wildlife viewing platform.
The Commission voted by roll call to authorize a purchase order for custom trail boundary markers, with a spending cap.
A new enforcement order will be issued for 23 Cove Road and closed once the shed is down and staff confirm; the owner said it will come down in spring.
The chair reviewed the timber rights fund, noting the timber harvest is not expected until mid-summer, so that revenue should not be counted on soon.
123 Farm Hill Road was removed from the encroachment list; 26 Lopez/Mopus Road stays on until inspected.

why_it_matters: Both purchases draw on the Commission's timber rights fund, and the fund's timber income is delayed, so spending on conservation land and trails is paid from a balance rather than from new harvest revenue.
The Cove Road order and the encroachment list show how the Commission enforces wetland and boundary rules on private property, which matters to neighbors of conservation land.
watch_next: The March 1st Commission meeting, where 48 Oak Ridge is scheduled and 454 Pine Grove still needs a full submittal.
The report on the Haws gift fund, to be prepared with Rebecca Manley, and the Ellis Road carpet quotes.
